words.defn_en: a microscopic single-celled organism, some of which cause disease:

sentences.en: Scientists identified a new ______ resistant to common antibiotics.
sentences.zh: 科學家發現了一種對常見抗生素具有抗藥性的新細菌。

sentences.en: A single ______ can multiply into millions within hours under the right conditions.
sentences.zh: 在適當的條件下,單一細菌能在幾小時內繁殖成數百萬個。

words.defn_en: a person who gullibly believes everything they read or hear:

sentences.en: The scam artist counted on finding a ______ willing to wire money to a stranger.
sentences.zh: 詐騙者仰賴找到一位輕信的人,願意匯款給一個陌生人。

sentences.en: Only a true ______ would believe that email claiming he'd won a foreign lottery.
sentences.zh: 只有真正輕信的人才會相信那封宣稱自己中了海外樂透的郵件。

words.defn_en: to pester, nag, annoy persistently:

sentences.en: The reporters continued to ______ the actor with questions about his divorce.
sentences.zh: 記者們不斷用有關他離婚的問題糾纏這位演員。

sentences.en: My little brother kept ______ing me to buy him a new video game.
sentences.zh: 我弟弟不停糾纏著要我買一款新的電動遊戲給他。

words.defn_en: frivolous banter:

sentences.en: The two old friends exchanged playful ______ over coffee.
sentences.zh: 這兩位老朋友一邊喝咖啡,一邊互相打趣說笑。

sentences.en: Their light ______ masked a much deeper conversation happening underneath.
sentences.zh: 他們表面上輕鬆的玩笑話,掩蓋了底下更深層的對話。

words.defn_en: to completely confuse or perplex:

sentences.en: The disappearing coin trick continued to ______ even seasoned magicians.
sentences.zh: 這個消失硬幣的把戲,連經驗豐富的魔術師都感到困惑。

sentences.en: The sudden drop in sales ______ the entire marketing team.
sentences.zh: 銷售額突然下滑,讓整個行銷團隊都摸不著頭緒。

words.defn_en: thing of little importance:

sentences.en: Compared to the company's huge losses, this expense was a mere ______.
sentences.zh: 與這家公司龐大的虧損相比,這筆開銷只是微不足道的小事。

sentences.en: He treated the missing sum as a ______, not worth mentioning.
sentences.zh: 他把這筆遺失的金額視為無關緊要的小事,不值一提。

words.defn_en: threatening harm; menacing:

sentences.en: The old house had a ______ presence that kept trick-or-treaters away.
sentences.zh: 這棟老房子散發著一股不祥的氣息,讓萬聖節討糖的孩子都不敢靠近。

sentences.en: He shot a ______ glance at the man who had crossed him.
sentences.zh: 他朝那個冒犯他的人投以凶狠的一瞥。

words.defn_en: to be unwilling, refuse:

sentences.en: Many customers ______ at the high price of the new phone.
sentences.zh: 許多顧客對這支新手機的高昂價格望而卻步。

sentences.en: He tends to ______ whenever asked to speak in front of a large crowd.
sentences.zh: 每當被要求在大批群眾面前發言,他總會猶豫退縮。

words.defn_en: a love song:

sentences.en: The singer closed the concert with a slow, emotional ______.
sentences.zh: 這位歌手以一首緩慢動人的情歌結束了這場演唱會。

sentences.en: The folk ______ told the tragic story of two star-crossed lovers.
sentences.zh: 這首民謠敘述了一對命運多舛的戀人的悲劇故事。

words.defn_en: a female ballet dancer:

sentences.en: The young ______ practiced her pirouettes for hours before the recital.
sentences.zh: 這位年輕芭蕾女伶在演出前練習了好幾個小時的旋轉動作。

sentences.en: Every ______ in the company dreamed of dancing the lead role in Swan Lake.
sentences.zh: 舞團裡的每一位芭蕾女伶都夢想能演出《天鵝湖》的主角。

words.defn_en: to trick or deceive someone:

sentences.en: The salesman tried to ______ customers with confusing warranty terms.
sentences.zh: 這位業務員試圖用令人困惑的保固條款來矇騙顧客。

sentences.en: She refused to be ______ by his flattering promises.
sentences.zh: 她拒絕被他那些花言巧語的承諾所矇騙。

words.defn_en: an official prohibition; to officially forbid:
words.root_note: bannan (to summon, proclaim, from Old English)

sentences.en: The city imposed a ______ on single-use plastic bags.
sentences.zh: 這座城市對一次性塑膠袋實施了禁令。

sentences.en: The league voted to ______ the substance after several athletes tested positive.
sentences.zh: 在數名選手驗出陽性反應後,聯盟投票決定禁用這種物質。

words.defn_en: commonplace or trite saying:

sentences.en: The film's dialogue felt ______ and predictable.
sentences.zh: 這部電影的台詞顯得平庸又老套。

sentences.en: He tried to avoid ______ small talk at the party.
sentences.zh: 他在派對上試圖避免陳腔濫調的閒聊。

words.defn_en: trite, unoriginal remarks or commonplaces:
words.root_note: banal, of uncertain further origin, related to Old French ban (feudal jurisdiction)

sentences.en: His speech was filled with tired ______ instead of fresh ideas.
sentences.zh: 他的演說充滿了老套的陳腔濫調,而非新穎的想法。

sentences.en: She grew tired of exchanging polite ______ at every party.
sentences.zh: 她厭倦了在每場派對上交換禮貌性的陳腔濫調。

words.defn_en: the quality of being dull, unoriginal, or overused:

sentences.en: The critic dismissed the film's dialogue as pure ______.
sentences.zh: 評論家批評這部電影的對白純粹是陳腔濫調。

sentences.en: Despite its ______ , the greeting card still made her smile.
sentences.zh: 儘管內容陳腐,這張賀卡仍讓她會心一笑。

words.defn_en: a robber or outlaw, especially one belonging to a gang:

sentences.en: The mountain pass was once notorious for ______ attacks on merchant caravans.
sentences.zh: 這處山口曾以強盜襲擊商隊而惡名昭彰。

sentences.en: The film follows a reformed ______ trying to protect his village.
sentences.zh: 這部電影講述一位改過自新的土匪,試圖保護自己村莊的故事。

words.defn_en: a burden:

sentences.en: Traffic during rush hour is the ______ of every commuter's existence.
sentences.zh: 尖峰時段的塞車是每位通勤者最大的困擾。

sentences.en: Procrastination has always been the ______ of his academic career.
sentences.zh: 拖延一直是他求學生涯中最大的絆腳石。

words.defn_en: causing ruin; harmful; pernicious

sentences.en: The ______ effects of the pesticide harmed local wildlife.
sentences.zh: 這種殺蟲劑造成的有害影響傷害了當地的野生動物。

sentences.en: His ______ influence on the young students worried the school administration.
sentences.zh: 他對這些年輕學生所帶來的有害影響讓校方感到憂心。

words.defn_en: playful, teasing conversation; to tease jokingly:

sentences.en: Friendly ______ between the two hosts kept the podcast lighthearted.
sentences.zh: 兩位主持人之間友善的戲謔,讓這個播客節目氣氛輕鬆。

sentences.en: The coworkers would ______ about sports every Monday morning.
sentences.zh: 同事們每週一早上都會就運動話題互相調侃。

words.defn_en: a rod or barrier; to prevent or forbid:

sentences.en: A metal ______ blocked the entrance to the closed section of the museum.
sentences.zh: 一根金屬橫木擋住了博物館關閉區域的入口。

sentences.en: The court moved to ______ the witness from testifying further.
sentences.zh: 法院決定禁止該名證人繼續作證。

words.defn_en: an outer defensive structure at the entrance to a castle or city:
words.root_note: barbacana (from Old French, of uncertain origin)

sentences.en: Archers once defended the ______ against any army approaching the castle gate.
sentences.zh: 弓箭手曾在這座外堡守衛,抵禦任何逼近城堡大門的軍隊。

sentences.en: Tourists can still climb the stone ______ that guards the old city walls.
sentences.zh: 遊客至今仍能爬上守護舊城牆的那座石造外堡。

words.defn_en: organic compound having powerful soporific effect:
words.defn_zh: 巴比妥類藥物(鎮靜安眠藥)

sentences.en: The doctor warned against mixing alcohol with any ______.
sentences.zh: 醫生警告不要將酒精與任何巴比妥類藥物混合服用。

sentences.en: ______s were once commonly prescribed for anxiety before safer alternatives were developed.
sentences.zh: 在更安全的替代藥物問世之前,巴比妥類藥物曾經是治療焦慮症的常見處方。

words.defn_en: a poet, often a singer as well:

sentences.en: The ancient ______ traveled from village to village telling tales in verse.
sentences.zh: 這位古代的吟遊詩人走遍村莊,以詩歌形式講述故事。

sentences.en: Shakespeare is often referred to simply as "the ______."
sentences.zh: 莎士比亞常被人們直接稱為「吟遊詩人」。

words.defn_en: instrument for measuring change:

sentences.en: Consumer spending is often seen as a ______ of the overall economy.
sentences.zh: 消費者支出常被視為整體經濟的一項晴雨表。

sentences.en: The sudden drop in the ______ signaled an approaching storm.
sentences.zh: 氣壓計的突然下降預示著暴風雨即將來臨。

words.defn_en: too poor to produce much vegetation; unable to produce offspring:
words.root_note: barhaine (from Old French, of uncertain origin)

sentences.en: After years of drought, the once-fertile fields had become completely ______.
sentences.zh: 經過多年乾旱,曾經肥沃的田地已完全變得貧瘠。

sentences.en: The novel follows a couple struggling with the grief of being ______.
sentences.zh: 這部小說描述一對夫妻在不孕的悲傷中掙扎的故事。

words.defn_en: an obstruction, especially one built hastily; to block with such a structure:

sentences.en: Protesters built a ______ out of overturned carts and furniture.
sentences.zh: 抗議者用翻倒的推車和家具築起了一道路障。

sentences.en: Police moved quickly to ______ the street after the accident.
sentences.zh: 警方在事故發生後迅速封鎖了這條街道。

words.defn_en: a small overhanging turret on a castle wall:

sentences.en: A lone guard once kept watch from the castle's stone ______.
sentences.zh: 曾有一名孤零零的守衛,從城堡的石造角樓上把守瞭望。

sentences.en: The restored ______ offers a stunning view of the surrounding countryside.
sentences.zh: 這座修復後的角樓,能俯瞰周圍鄉間美不勝收的景色。

words.defn_en: the lowest part or foundation; morally low or dishonorable:

sentences.en: Engineers reinforced the ______ of the bridge before winter set in.
sentences.zh: 冬季來臨前,工程師強化了這座橋的橋基。

sentences.en: His ______ betrayal of a lifelong friend shocked everyone who knew him.
sentences.zh: 他對摯友卑劣的背叛,震驚了所有認識他的人。

words.defn_en: the quality of being morally low or dishonorable:

sentences.en: The novel exposes the ______ hidden beneath the family's respectable reputation.
sentences.zh: 這部小說揭露了這個家族體面聲譽背後隱藏的卑劣。

sentences.en: Few could imagine such ______ from someone once admired as a hero.
sentences.zh: 很少人能想像一個曾被視為英雄的人,竟會如此卑劣。

words.defn_en: shy, excessively timid:

sentences.en: The ______ boy hid behind his mother whenever a stranger spoke to him.
sentences.zh: 每當有陌生人跟他說話,這個害羞的男孩就會躲到媽媽身後。

sentences.en: Despite being famous, the actress remained surprisingly ______ in interviews.
sentences.zh: 儘管聲名遠播,這位女演員在訪談中依然出奇地靦腆。

words.defn_en: shyness or timidity, especially in social situations:
words.root_note: bashen (to be astonished, from Middle English)

sentences.en: Her ______ made it hard for her to speak up in large meetings.
sentences.zh: 她的害羞讓她很難在大型會議上發言。

sentences.en: The teacher gently encouraged the child to overcome his ______.
sentences.zh: 老師溫柔地鼓勵這個孩子克服自己的靦腆。

words.defn_en: the foundation or fundamental principle of something:

sentences.en: Mutual trust formed the ______ of their long partnership.
sentences.zh: 相互信任構成了他們長久合作關係的基礎。

sentences.en: The lawsuit had no legal ______ and was dismissed within a week.
sentences.zh: 這起訴訟毫無法律依據,一週內就被駁回。

words.defn_en: excessively sentimental in a way that seems unintentionally comic:

sentences.en: The film's ______ ending drew more laughter than tears from the audience.
sentences.zh: 這部電影矯情的結局,引來的是觀眾的笑聲而非淚水。

sentences.en: Critics mocked the singer's ______ lyrics about lost love.
sentences.zh: 評論家嘲笑這位歌手那些關於失戀、假悲情的歌詞。

words.defn_en: an abrupt, often unintentional shift from a serious tone to a trivial or comic one:

sentences.en: The tragic speech collapsed into ______ when the microphone suddenly squeaked.
sentences.zh: 麥克風突然發出刺耳聲響,讓這場悲壯的演講瞬間淪為滑稽。

sentences.en: The playwright uses ______ deliberately, undercutting tension with a silly joke.
sentences.zh: 這位劇作家刻意運用這種虎頭蛇尾的手法,用一個蠢笑話化解緊張氣氛。

words.defn_en: a device that supplies power:

sentences.en: The remote control stopped working because the ______ died.
sentences.zh: 這支遙控器因為電池沒電而無法使用了。

sentences.en: He faced criminal charges after the ______ incident outside the bar.
sentences.zh: 在酒吧外發生毆打事件後,他面臨刑事指控。

words.defn_en: a parapet with gaps for defense, built on top of a wall:

sentences.en: Guards patrolled the ______ throughout the night, watching for approaching enemies.
sentences.zh: 守衛整夜在城垛上巡邏,警戒逼近的敵人。

sentences.en: Tourists can walk along the restored ______ of the medieval castle.
sentences.zh: 遊客可以沿著這座中世紀城堡修復後的城垛漫步。

words.defn_en: to repeat needlessly in speech or writing:
words.root_note: battologia (from Battos, a stammering king), from Greek

sentences.en: The professor tended to ______ his main point until students tuned out entirely.
sentences.zh: 這位教授總愛把重點囉唆地重複,直到學生完全失去興趣。

sentences.en: Good editors cut passages where a writer seems to ______ the same idea.
sentences.zh: 優秀的編輯會刪去作者對同一觀點反覆贅述的段落。

words.defn_en: a small, showy trinket or decoration of little value:

sentences.en: The market stall was covered in cheap ______ that sparkled under the lights.
sentences.zh: 這個市集攤位上擺滿了在燈光下閃閃發亮的廉價小飾品。

sentences.en: He dismissed the antique ring as a worthless ______ , not realizing its true value.
sentences.zh: 他把這枚古董戒指當成不值錢的小玩意,卻不知道它的真正價值。

words.defn_en: humorously indecent or crude, especially about sex:
words.root_note: bawd (a person who runs a brothel, from Old French)

sentences.en: The comedian's ______ jokes were not suitable for the family show.
sentences.zh: 這位喜劇演員粗俗詼諧的笑話,並不適合闔家觀賞的節目。

sentences.en: Shakespeare's plays are full of ______ humor that modern audiences sometimes miss.
sentences.zh: 莎士比亞的劇作充滿粗俗詼諧的幽默,現代觀眾有時會忽略這一點。

words.defn_en: unpleasant or cruel, like a beast:

sentences.en: The weather turned ______ the moment the hikers reached the summit.
sentences.zh: 登山客一抵達山頂,天氣就變得極為惡劣。

sentences.en: His ______ treatment of the staff eventually led to his dismissal.
sentences.zh: 他對員工殘暴的對待,最終導致他被解雇。

words.defn_en: blissfully happy; showing serene joy:

sentences.en: A ______ smile spread across her face as she held her newborn.
sentences.zh: 抱著剛出生的孩子,她臉上洋溢著幸福的笑容。

sentences.en: The monk's ______ expression suggested a lifetime of inner peace.
sentences.zh: 這位僧人臉上至福的神情,彷彿映照著一生的內心平靜。

words.defn_en: supreme blessedness or happiness:

sentences.en: The old hymn speaks of a ______ found only after life's struggles.
sentences.zh: 這首古老的聖歌訴說著唯有經歷人生磨難後才能尋得的至福。

sentences.en: She described the mountain sunrise as a moment of pure ______.
sentences.zh: 她形容山頂日出的那一刻,是純粹無上的幸福。

words.defn_en: a man who is excessively concerned with fashion and appearance; a dandy:
words.root_note: from Beau Brummell, a famous English dandy

sentences.en: His closet full of tailored suits made him the office's resident ______.
sentences.zh: 他衣櫃裡滿是量身訂製的西裝,讓他成了辦公室裡公認的時髦男子。

sentences.en: The novel's ______ character cares more about his cravat than the coming war.
sentences.zh: 這部小說中的花花公子角色,在乎自己的領巾遠勝過即將爆發的戰爭。

words.defn_en: fashionable society; the world of the elegant and wealthy:

sentences.en: The gallery opening drew the city's entire ______ , dressed in their finest.
sentences.zh: 這場畫廊開幕吸引了全城的上流人士,個個盛裝出席。

sentences.en: She wrote a gossip column chronicling the scandals of the local ______.
sentences.zh: 她撰寫的八卦專欄,記錄了當地上流社會的種種醜聞。

words.defn_en: to make something more attractive:

sentences.en: Volunteers planted flowers to ______ the neglected park.
sentences.zh: 志工們種植花朵,美化這座乏人照顧的公園。

sentences.en: The city council approved funds to ______ the crumbling downtown plaza.
sentences.zh: 市議會核准了經費,用以美化這處日漸破敗的市中心廣場。

words.defn_en: to make a sailing ship unable to move due to lack of wind; to calm:
words.defn_zh: 使(船)因無風而停滯;使平靜

sentences.en: The ship was ______ for three days in the middle of the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 這艘船在太平洋中央因無風而停滯了三天。

sentences.en: Her gentle voice managed to ______ the frightened child.
sentences.zh: 她溫柔的聲音成功讓受驚的孩子平靜下來。

words.defn_en: to smear or cover with something messy:

sentences.en: The toddler managed to ______ the entire kitchen wall with spaghetti sauce.
sentences.zh: 這個小孩把整面廚房牆壁都抹上了義大利麵醬。

sentences.en: Protesters would often ______ statues with paint to make a political statement.
sentences.zh: 抗議者常會在雕像上塗抹油漆,以表達政治訴求。

words.defn_en: to make dim or obscure:

sentences.en: Thick fog began to ______ the harbor lights.
sentences.zh: 濃霧開始讓港口的燈光變得昏暗不明。

sentences.en: Age had begun to ______ the once-vivid colors of the old mural.
sentences.zh: 歲月讓這幅曾經色彩鮮豔的壁畫逐漸黯淡模糊。

words.defn_en: uproar, confusion:

sentences.en: The stadium erupted into ______ when the home team scored.
sentences.zh: 當主場球隊得分時,整座體育館陷入一片混亂喧鬧。

sentences.en: The classroom descended into ______ the moment the teacher stepped out.
sentences.zh: 老師一離開教室,班上立刻陷入一片混亂。

words.defn_en: to confuse or perplex:

sentences.en: The instructions were so complicated they managed to ______ even the technician.
sentences.zh: 這份說明書複雜到連技師都被搞得一頭霧水。

sentences.en: Jet lag can ______ even the most experienced travelers.
sentences.zh: 時差可能連經驗最豐富的旅人都會感到迷糊。
